passages.text: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
This happened in the tenth year.
It was the twelfth day of the tenth month.
The LORD said these words to me.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me to look toward Pharaoh.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
God told me to prophesy against Pharaoh.
God told me to prophesy against all Egypt.
passages.original: בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔ית בָּעֲשִׂרִ֕י בִּשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֣ים פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־ פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִנָּבֵ֣א עָלָ֔יו וְעַל־ מִצְרַ֖יִם כֻּלָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Speak to him and tell him that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Pharaoh king of Egypt, O great monster who lies among his rivers, who says, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it myself.’
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD spoke to Ezekiel.
The Lord told Ezekiel to speak to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh was proud and powerful.
Pharaoh acted like a great monster.
This monster lay among his rivers.
Pharaoh said, “The Nile is mine.”
Pharaoh claimed, “I made the Nile myself.”
The Lord GOD said, “I am against you, Pharaoh.”
passages.original: דַּבֵּ֨ר וְאָמַרְתָּ֜ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְנִ֤י עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם הַתַּנִּים֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל הָרֹבֵ֖ץ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְאֹרָ֑יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמַ֛ר לִ֥י יְאֹרִ֖י וַאֲנִ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽנִי׃

passages.text: But I will put hooks in your jaws and cause the fish of your streams to cling to your scales. I will haul you up out of your rivers, and all the fish of your streams will cling to your scales.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God addressed Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
God called Pharaoh a great monster who lies among his rivers.
God said, “I will act against you, Pharaoh.”
God said, “I will put hooks in your jaws.”
God said, “I will make the fish of your rivers stick to your scales.”
God said, “I will pull you out of your rivers.”
God said, “All the fish of your rivers will cling to your scales.”
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֤י חַחִיִּים בִּלְחָיֶ֔יךָ וְהִדְבַּקְתִּ֥י דְגַת־ יְאֹרֶ֖יךָ בְּקַשְׂקְשֹׂתֶ֑יךָ וְהַעֲלִיתִ֙יךָ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ דְּגַ֣ת יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ בְּקַשְׂקְשֹׂתֶ֖יךָ תִּדְבָּֽק׃

passages.text: I will leave you in the desert, you and all the fish of your streams. You will fall on the open field and will not be taken away or gathered for burial. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the air.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Pharaoh is proud and claims the Nile as his own.
God says, "I will leave you in the desert."
You will be there with all the fish of your streams.
You will fall on the open field.
No one will take you away.
No one will gather you for burial.
I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth.
I have given you as food to the birds of the air.
passages.original: וּנְטַשְׁתִּ֣יךָ הַמִּדְבָּ֗רָה אוֹתְךָ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ דְּגַ֣ת יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ עַל־ פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ תִּפּ֔וֹל לֹ֥א תֵאָסֵ֖ף וְלֹ֣א תִקָּבֵ֑ץ לְחַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֛רֶץ וּלְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נְתַתִּ֥יךָ לְאָכְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Then all the people of Egypt will know that I am the LORD. For you were only a staff of reeds to the house of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Egypt.
God said, “I am the LORD.”
All the people living in Egypt will know this.
Egypt was a staff made of reeds.
Egypt was weak and unreliable.
Egypt was a staff for the house of Israel.
Egypt could not support Israel.
passages.original: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה יַ֧עַן הֱיוֹתָ֛ם מִשְׁעֶ֥נֶת קָנֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: When Israel took hold of you with their hands, you splintered, tearing all their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke, and their backs were wrenched.
passages.sermon:
Egypt was like a staff of reeds to Israel.
Israel tried to take hold of Egypt for support.
Israel grabbed Egypt with their hands.
Egypt splintered.
Egypt tore all their shoulders.
Israel leaned on Egypt for help.
Egypt broke.
Egypt caused all their backs to be wrenched.
passages.original: בְּתָפְשָׂ֨ם בְּךָ֤ בַכַּפְךָ תֵּר֔וֹץ וּבָקַעְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם כָּל־ כָּתֵ֑ף וּבְהִֽשָּׁעֲנָ֤ם עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם כָּל־ מָתְנָֽיִם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will bring a sword against you and cut off from you man and beast.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is the one true God.
He speaks to Egypt.
He says, “I will bring a sword against you, Egypt.”
I will remove people from you.
I will remove animals from you.
No man or beast will remain.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלַ֖יִךְ חָ֑רֶב וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֵּ֖ךְ אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: The land of Egypt will become a desolate wasteland. Then they will know that I am the LORD. Because you said, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it,’ therefore I am against you and against your rivers. I will turn the land of Egypt into a ruin, a desolate wasteland from Migdol to Syene, and as far as the border of Cush.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God spoke to Egypt.
God said the land of Egypt will become a desolate wasteland.
Egypt will be empty and ruined.
The people will know that God is the LORD.
Egypt said, “The Nile is mine. I made it.”
God heard Egypt’s pride.
God said, “I am against you, Egypt. I am against your rivers.”
God will make the land of Egypt a ruin.
Egypt will be a desolate wasteland.
This wasteland will stretch from Migdol to Syene.
It will reach as far as the border of Cush.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָ֤ה אֶֽרֶץ־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֣ה וְחָרְבָּ֔ה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר יְאֹ֥ר לִ֖י וַאֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי׃ לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְאֶל־ יְאֹרֶ֑יךָ וְנָתַתִּ֞י אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם לְחָרְבוֹת֙ חֹ֣רֶב שְׁמָמָ֔ה מִמִּגְדֹּ֥ל סְוֵנֵ֖ה וְעַד־ גְּב֥וּל כּֽוּשׁ׃

passages.text: No foot of man or beast will pass through, and it will be uninhabited for forty years.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking about Egypt.
God says Egypt will become empty and ruined.
No person will walk through Egypt.
No animal will walk through Egypt.
No one will live in Egypt for forty years.
passages.original: לֹ֤א תַעֲבָר־ בָּהּ֙ רֶ֣גֶל אָדָ֔ם וְרֶ֥גֶל בְּהֵמָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַעֲבָר־ בָּ֑הּ וְלֹ֥א תֵשֵׁ֖ב אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities will lie desolate for forty years among the ruined cities. And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God will act against Egypt.
God will make the land of Egypt empty and ruined.
Egypt will become a desolation.
Other lands around Egypt will also be desolate.
The cities of Egypt will be ruined.
These cities will stay empty for forty years.
God will scatter the people of Egypt.
God will send the Egyptians among many nations.
God will spread them out in different countries.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־ אֶרֶץ֩ מִצְרַ֨יִם שְׁמָמָ֜ה בְּת֣וֹךְ׀ אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֗וֹת וְעָרֶ֙יהָ֙ בְּת֨וֹךְ עָרִ֤ים מָֽחֳרָבוֹת֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֣יןָ שְׁמָמָ֔ה אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַהֲפִצֹתִ֤י אֶת־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְֽזֵרִיתִ֖ים בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations to which they were scattered.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority.
The Lord GOD makes a promise about Egypt.
Egypt is a nation that was scattered among many nations.
The Lord GOD says He will act after forty years.
At the end of forty years, the Lord GOD will gather the Egyptians.
He will gather them from the nations where they were scattered.
passages.original: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה מִקֵּ֞ץ אַרְבָּעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אֲקַבֵּ֣ץ אֶת־ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִן־ הָעַמִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־ נָפֹ֥צוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: I will restore Egypt from captivity and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin. There they will be a lowly kingdom.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Egypt.
God says He will restore Egypt from captivity.
God will bring the Egyptians back to their own land.
Their land is Pathros.
Pathros is the land where they came from.
In Pathros, Egypt will become a lowly kingdom.
passages.original: וְשַׁבְתִּי֙ אֶת־ שְׁב֣וּת מִצְרַ֔יִם וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֤י אֹתָם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פַּתְר֔וֹס עַל־ אֶ֖רֶץ מְכֽוּרָתָ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ שָׁ֖ם מַמְלָכָ֥ה שְׁפָלָֽה׃

passages.text: Egypt will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again exalt itself above the nations. For I will diminish Egypt so that it will never again rule over the nations.
passages.sermon:
Egypt is a kingdom.
Egypt will be the lowest of all kingdoms.
Egypt will never lift itself up above other nations again.
I will make Egypt small.
Egypt will never rule over the nations again.
passages.original: מִן־ הַמַּמְלָכוֹת֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה שְׁפָלָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ תִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א ע֖וֹד עַל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְהִ֨מְעַטְתִּ֔ים לְבִלְתִּ֖י רְד֥וֹת בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: Egypt will never again be an object of trust for the house of Israel, but will remind them of their iniquity in turning to the Egyptians. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.”
passages.sermon:
Egypt will never again be a source of trust for the house of Israel.
Egypt will remind Israel of their sin.
Israel sinned by turning to Egypt for help.
Then Israel will know that I am the Lord GOD.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ עוֹד֩ לְבֵ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל לְמִבְטָח֙ מַזְכִּ֣יר עָוֺ֔ן בִּפְנוֹתָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

passages.text: In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to labor strenuously against Tyre. Every head was made bald and every shoulder made raw. But he and his army received no wages from Tyre for the labor they expended on it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
This happened in the twenty-seventh year.
It was the first day of the first month.
The LORD said these words to me.
He called me “Son of man.”
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar made his army work very hard against Tyre.
Every soldier’s head became bald.
Every soldier’s shoulder became raw.
Nebuchadnezzar and his army did not receive any wages from Tyre.
They received nothing for all their hard work against Tyre.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֙בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בָּֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּ֠בֶל הֶעֱבִ֨יד אֶת־ חֵיל֜וֹ עֲבֹדָ֤ה גְדֹלָה֙ אֶל־ צֹ֔ר כָּל־ רֹ֣אשׁ מֻקְרָ֔ח וְכָל־ כָּתֵ֖ף מְרוּטָ֑ה וְ֠שָׂכָר לֹא־ הָ֨יָה ל֤וֹ וּלְחֵילוֹ֙ מִצֹּ֔ר עַל־ הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָבַ֥ד עָלֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who will carry off its wealth, seize its spoil, and remove its plunder. This will be the wages for his army.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says this.
I will give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar.
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
He will take Egypt’s wealth.
He will seize Egypt’s spoil.
He will remove Egypt’s plunder.
This will be the wages for Nebuchadnezzar’s army.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן לִנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָשָׂ֨א הֲמֹנָ֜הּ וְשָׁלַ֤ל שְׁלָלָהּ֙ וּבָזַ֣ז בִּזָּ֔הּ וְהָיְתָ֥ה שָׂכָ֖ר לְחֵילֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have given him the land of Egypt as the reward for his labor, because it was done for Me, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD gave the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
This was a reward for Nebuchadnezzar’s labor.
Nebuchadnezzar and his army worked for the Lord GOD.
The Lord GOD declares this.
passages.original: פְּעֻלָּתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁר־ עָ֣בַד בָּ֔הּ נָתַ֥תִּי ל֖וֹ אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס

passages.text: In that day I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth to speak among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He promises to act on a certain day.
On that day, God will give strength to the house of Israel.
God will make a "horn" grow for Israel.
A "horn" means power and victory.
God will also give you the ability to speak among the people.
You will speak clearly in their midst.
The people will listen to your words.
They will know that I am the LORD.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אַצְמִ֤יחַ קֶ֙רֶן֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּלְךָ֛ אֶתֵּ֥ן פִּתְחֽוֹן־ פֶּ֖ה בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
